# Moldova: personal income tax (2026) v0.2

Moldova taxes individuals at one flat rate of 12% under Title II of the Fiscal Code. The State Tax Service (Serviciul Fiscal de Stat, SFS) collects the tax. The tax year is the calendar year (Fiscal Code art. 12^1(1)). Figures below are from the consolidated Fiscal Code on legis.md as amended to Law LP235 of 2 October 2026 (in force 30 October 2026), and from the amending laws of 2025 that took effect on 1 January 2026.

## Who this applies to

- **Residents.** An individual is resident if he or she has a permanent home (domiciliu permanent) in Moldova, including while abroad for treatment, rest, study or a business trip, or is in Moldova for at least 183 days in the tax year (art. 5 pct. 5 a)).
- **Who is taxed on what** (art. 13, 14):
  - Resident individual entrepreneurs, people providing professional services, and justice and health professionals: income from all sources, in Moldova and abroad.
  - Resident Moldovan citizens without a business: taxable income from Moldovan sources and from foreign sources for their work in Moldova, plus investment and financial income from abroad.
  - Resident foreigners and stateless persons working in Moldova: Moldovan-source income and foreign income for their work in Moldova, but not foreign investment and financial income.
  - Non-residents without a business in Moldova: only the Moldovan-source income listed in chapter 11 (art. 71).
- **Separate regimes inside Title II.** Justice and health professionals (chapter 10^1, art. 69^1 to 69^5), independent retail traders (chapter 10^2), plant-product buyers (chapter 10^3) and independent entrepreneurs (chapter 10^4, from 1 January 2026) have their own rules, shown below.
- **Out of this skill.** Companies (see [md-corporate-income-tax](md-corporate-income-tax.md)), the month-by-month payroll run (see [moldova-payroll](moldova-payroll.md)), social and health contributions (see [moldova-social-contributions](moldova-social-contributions.md)), VAT (see [moldova-vat](moldova-vat.md)), and IT park residents, whose staff salaries are taxed inside the 7% single tax (art. 370, 377; see [moldova-tax-optimization](moldova-tax-optimization.md)).

## The taxable base

**Gross income.** Gross income includes business and professional income, pay for work and services (salaries, employer benefits, fees, commissions, bonuses), rent, capital gains under art. 40(7), interest, royalties, annuities and insurance payouts not reinvested, debts written off by a creditor, state prizes not exempted, contract penalties received, and any other income not made non-taxable (art. 18). The non-taxable list is in art. 20. Each taxpayer must declare gross income from all sources (art. 13(2)).

**Business deductions.** An individual entrepreneur deducts the expenses of the business under chapter 3 of Title II (art. 24 onward). Justice and health professionals deduct business expenses under the same chapter and keep the exemptions in chapter 4 (art. 69^3). A fixed asset is depreciable when its value is above MDL 12,000 and its life is over one year, by the straight-line method; most businesses may instead deduct up to 50% of cost in the first year (art. 26^1(2), (6), (6^1)). Donations to public bodies, non-profits and unions are deductible up to 5% of taxable income (art. 36(1)-(2)).

**Losses.** A business loss is carried forward and spread over the next five tax years, oldest loss first (art. 32).

**Personal exemptions.** A resident whose annual taxable income is below MDL 360,000 (not counting income taxed finally under art. 90^1) gets the personal exemption of MDL 29,700, or MDL 34,620 for the groups in art. 33(2) (art. 33(1)-(2)). Income under the retail and plant-buyer regimes counts toward the MDL 360,000 test (art. 33(1^1)). The spouse exemption (art. 34(2)) and dependant exemptions (art. 35) start in the month after the right arises. A dependant is a parent or child of the taxpayer or spouse (including adoptive), or a second-degree collateral relative disabled from birth or childhood, whose own income is not above MDL 12,400 a year (art. 35(2)). Curators of minors aged 14 to 18 and legal guardians get the dependant exemption for each person in their care (art. 35(3)).

**Who loses the exemptions.** A person whose income was taxed for part of the year under the special regime in chapter 1 of Title X (IT park) cannot use the exemptions for that period; exemptions apply pro rata to the months under the standard regime (art. 35^1).

**Personal deductions.** An individual also deducts (art. 35^2):
- compulsory health insurance premiums he or she paid;
- compulsory state social insurance contributions he or she paid;
- voluntary health insurance or medical services from one provider, up to one forecast average monthly wage (MDL 17,400 for 2026);
- premiums under life, health, fire and natural-disaster insurance contracts, up to one average monthly wage for all contracts together;
- interest on a loan for a first home (not under state programmes), up to one average monthly wage, shared by co-owners in proportion to their shares;
- from 1 January 2026, own education or professional training and children's education at institutions under art. 15 of the Education Code, up to MDL 20,000 in total.

**Final withholding.** Dividends, bank interest, rent, royalties, winnings, donated money, plant and livestock produce sold in natural form (6%) and consignment sales (12%) taxed under art. 90^1 are final. They are not added to gross income and do not go on the return (art. 90^1(4)). The SFS may check plant and livestock sales and certain non-taxable income above MDL 100,000 a year (art. 90^1(5)).

**Rent to tenants who do not withhold.** An owner without a business who lets real estate to a person who is not a withholding agent (for example another individual) pays 7% of the monthly contract value himself. The contract must be registered with the SFS within 7 days of signing, and the tax is paid by the 25th of the current month. If the contract is not registered and the tax not paid, the SFS estimates the income by indirect methods (art. 90^1(3^4)).

**Services by a person without a business.** Income of an individual without a business from services or works, and fees of board and audit-committee members, are treated as salary and taxed at 12% by the payer (art. 88(5)). A director's mandate is treated as employment (art. 88(6)). An independent entrepreneur working for a client outside the conditions of art. 24(11^1) is treated as an employee (art. 88(8)).

**Independent retail regime (chapter 10^2).** A resident trader without a legal form, selling retail (no excise goods) from an outlet up to 50 m2, with income up to MDL 1,200,000 a year, may opt in by application to the SFS. Tax is 1% of sales, at least MDL 3,000 a year; on stopping mid-year, at least MDL 250 for each month of activity. The SFS sends quarterly payment notices by the 25th of the month after each quarter, at least MDL 750 for quarters I to III, with a recalculation in Q4. The first year's tax is reduced by the cost of the cash register, unless already compensated. A cash register connected to the SFS sales-monitoring system is mandatory (art. 69^6 to 69^12).

**Independent entrepreneurs (chapter 10^4, from 1 January 2026).** A resident individual registered with the Public Services Agency as an independent entrepreneur (antreprenor independent) may provide only the services listed in the annex to chapter 10^4 (40 activities, including software development 62.01, IT consulting 62.02, data processing and web portals 63.1, design 74.1, translation 74.3, architecture 71.11 and engineering 71.12). There is no bookkeeping and no return: the SFS records income from cash-register data and the dedicated bank accounts (art. 69^22). The single tax is 15% of income up to MDL 1,200,000 a year and 35% on the excess. It includes income tax, state social insurance contributions, compulsory health insurance premiums and local taxes (art. 69^25). Independent entrepreneurs are not required to register for VAT (art. 112(1)). Chapter 10^4 was added by Law LP228/2025, in force 1 January 2026.

## Deadlines and filing

| What | Deadline | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Annual income tax return of individuals | 30 April of the following year (30 April 2027 for 2026) | art. 83(4) b) |
| Annual income tax return of legal persons and of resident organisational forms with the status of an individual | the 25th of the third month after the tax year (25 March 2027 for 2026) | art. 83(4) a) |
| Payment of the annual tax | by the return deadline, without extensions | art. 87(1) |
| Unified annual return of an individual entrepreneur or farm with up to 5 staff on average and not VAT-registered | 25 March of the following year | art. 83(11), 92(8) |
| Justice and health professionals: return | 25 March of the following year | art. 69^5(4) |
| Justice and health professionals: tax instalments | by the 25th of the month after each quarter | art. 69^5(2) |
| Business taxpayers (agenţi economici): instalments | 25 March, 25 June, 25 September, 25 December, each 1/4 of this year's estimate or of last year's tax | art. 84(1) |
| Farms: instalments | 1/4 by 25 September and 3/4 by 25 December | art. 84(2) |
| Owner's 7% tax on real-estate rent | register the contract within 7 days; pay by the 25th of the current month | art. 90^1(3^4) |
| Tax withheld by payers | by the 25th of the following month | art. 92(1) |
| Independent entrepreneur | SFS notice by the 10th, payment by the 25th of the following month | art. 69^26(2) |
| Independent retail trader | SFS notice and payment by the 25th of the month after each quarter | art. 69^12(2) |

**Who must file** (art. 83(2)): individuals with tax to pay; everyone in professional activity, even with no tax due; residents who used the personal exemption and had annual taxable income above MDL 360,000 (not counting art. 90^1 income); residents who direct a percentage of their tax to a beneficiary; non-residents with income under art. 74; and individual entrepreneurs and farms. A person who is not obliged to file may file to reclaim overpaid tax (art. 83(5)). Someone who moves his permanent home abroad files a return for the part of the year he was resident (art. 83(7)). An individual without a business may ask the SFS, before the deadline, to extend the filing date (art. 83(8)). Returns of individual entrepreneurs and professionals are filed electronically (art. 83(12), 69^5(6)). The form of the return is set by the Ministry of Finance (art. 83(4)); it is commonly called CET18.

**Information from payers.** By 1 March, every payer gives the individual a statement of income paid, exemptions and deductions applied and tax withheld (art. 92(4)).

## Penalties and interest

| Breach | Penalty | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Late payment | interest for each day from the due date to the payment date; for 2026, NBM base rate 6% + 5 points = 11% a year, divided by the days in the year | art. 228(2)-(3) |
| Corrected return showing more tax | interest under art. 228, capped at the extra tax | art. 228(2^1) |
| Return not filed or not filed correctly | MDL 200 to 400 per return (cap MDL 2,000) or MDL 500 to 1,000 per return (cap MDL 10,000), depending on the taxpayer group in art. 232 | art. 260(1) |
| Tax, contributions or premiums reduced by false data in a return | 20% to 30% of the amount reduced; not applied when the taxpayer corrects the return himself | art. 261(4), (4^1) |
| Evading calculation and payment | 80% to 100% of the undeclared amount | art. 261(5) |
| Instalments unpaid or underpaid | a fine at the art. 228(3) rate between the instalment date and the return date; the instalment due is the lower of last year's tax and 80% of this year's tax; not applied if the instalment due is below MDL 5,000 | art. 261(6) |
| False information in an exemption application to the employer | a fine and criminal liability under the law | art. 88(4) |

The SFS may assess tax, interest and fines for 4 years from the filing or payment date, and up to 6 years if no return was filed or a refund is claimed (art. 264(1), (3)).

## Cross-border points

- **Non-residents.** A non-resident individual without a business in Moldova is taxed only on Moldovan-source income in art. 71, for example payments for services provided in Moldova, management and consulting fees paid by a resident, dividends and interest paid by residents, and capital gains on assets located or registered in Moldova (art. 71(1)). The payer withholds 12%, or 6% on dividends (art. 91(1)). Non-residents receiving income from payers who do not withhold are taxed under art. 74 and file a return (art. 74, 83(2) b1)). Real-estate rent received by a non-resident from such a payer is taxed at 12% of the monthly contract value, with the contract registered within 7 days (art. 74(1^1)).
- **Residents with foreign income.** Residents are taxed on worldwide income as set out in art. 13. Tax paid abroad is credited under art. 82 (for justice and health professionals, art. 69^5(3)).
- **Leaving Moldova.** A person moving abroad files a return for the resident part of the year (art. 83(7)).
- **Treaties.** Treaty rates and the documents needed to apply them are in art. 79^3 and the individual treaties; see the pack's cross-border skill, [md-cross-border](md-cross-border.md).

## Worked examples

**Example 1. Employee, 2026, standard exemption.** A resident employee earns MDL 240,000 gross in 2026 (MDL 20,000 a month) and has no other income. The 9% health insurance premium withheld by the employer, MDL 21,600, is deductible (art. 35^2(1)). Employees pay no state social insurance contribution, so there is nothing more to deduct. Income after the deduction is MDL 218,400, below MDL 360,000, so the MDL 29,700 personal exemption applies (art. 33(1)). Taxable income is MDL 188,700 and the tax at 12% is MDL 22,644. If the employer withheld exactly this over the year, no return is needed (art. 83(2)).

```oa-check
name: Moldova employee, MDL 240,000 gross, 2026
inputs:
  gross: 240000
  health_rate: 0.09
  personal_exemption: 29700
  pit_rate: 0.12
steps:
  - health: gross * health_rate
  - income_after_deductions: gross - health
  - taxable: income_after_deductions - personal_exemption
  - tax: taxable * pit_rate
expected:
  health: 21600
  income_after_deductions: 218400
  taxable: 188700
  tax: 22644
```

**Example 2. Individual entrepreneur above the exemption limit, with bank interest.** A resident individual entrepreneur has business profit of MDL 420,000 in 2026 after business expenses. She also receives MDL 10,000 of bank interest, from which the bank withheld the final 6%, MDL 600 (art. 90^1(3^7)); the interest stays off the return (art. 90^1(4)). She paid the fixed state social insurance contribution of MDL 22,878 (see moldova-social-contributions). As the founder of an individual enterprise she paid the fixed health premium by 31 March, so she paid the reduced MDL 2,527 rather than MDL 12,636. Both are deductible (art. 35^2(1)-(2)). Her taxable income is MDL 394,595. That is above MDL 360,000, so she gets no personal exemption (art. 33(1)). Tax at 12% is MDL 47,351.40. She has no staff and is not VAT-registered, so she files the unified return by 25 March 2027 (art. 83(11)).

```oa-check
name: Moldova individual entrepreneur, profit MDL 420,000, no exemption, 2026
inputs:
  profit: 420000
  social_fixed: 22878
  health_fixed_paid_by_31_march: 2527
  bank_interest: 10000
  pit_rate: 0.12
  interest_final_rate: 0.06
  exemption_limit: 360000
steps:
  - interest_tax_withheld: bank_interest * interest_final_rate
  - taxable: profit - social_fixed - health_fixed_paid_by_31_march
  - over_limit: taxable - exemption_limit
  - tax: taxable * pit_rate
expected:
  interest_tax_withheld: 600
  taxable: 394595
  over_limit: 34595
  tax: 47351.40
```

## Ask the client first

1. Where is your permanent home, and how many days were you in Moldova in 2026?
2. What kinds of income did you have: salary, business, professional fees, rent, dividends, interest, foreign income? Who paid each one, and was tax withheld?
3. Do you run a business, and under which form: individual enterprise, farm, justice or health practice, retail trader, independent entrepreneur, IT park company?
4. Is your annual taxable income near or above MDL 360,000?
5. Do you support dependants, or do you or your spouse fall into a group with the higher MDL 34,620 exemption?
6. Did you pay for education, voluntary health insurance, life insurance or first-home loan interest in 2026?

# Moldova: social and health contributions (2026) v0.2

Moldova has two compulsory systems. State social insurance (asigurări sociale de stat, run by the National Social Insurance House, CNAS) is set by Law 489/1999 on the public social insurance system and the yearly state social insurance budget law (for 2026, Law LP320 of 29 December 2025). Compulsory health insurance (asigurare obligatorie de asistenţă medicală, run by the National Health Insurance Company, CNAM) is set by Law 1593/2002 and the yearly health insurance funds law (for 2026, Law LP321 of 29 December 2025). The State Tax Service (SFS) collects the percentage contributions and premiums.

## Who this applies to

- **Employers** pay state social insurance on salaries and other rewards of employees and of people working under civil contracts for works or services (Law 489/1999 annex 1 pt. 1.1).
- **Employees** pay no state social insurance contribution; the annex has employer lines only (annex 1 pt. 1.1). Employees and other people receiving rewards pay the 9% health premium, which the payer withholds (Law 1593/2002 annex 1 pt. 2 and 4; Law LP321/2025 art. 4(1)).
- **People insured on their own** pay fixed annual amounts: founders of individual enterprises and farms, independent retail traders, plant-product buyers and patent holders (annex 1 pt. 1.6, 1.7), justice professionals (pt. 1.6^1), and people under an individual contract with CNAS (LP320/2025 art. 3(3)). Pensioners and people with disabilities are outside pt. 1.6, 1.6^1 and 1.7.
- **Health premium in a fixed sum**: unemployed residents who own or rent agricultural land, founders of individual enterprises, patent holders, independent retail traders, people renting out property, plant-product buyers, justice professionals, family doctors in independent practice, and other residents who are neither employed nor insured by the Government (Law 1593/2002 annex 2).
- **Carve-outs.** IT park residents pay social insurance under Law 77/2016 inside their single tax (annex 1 pt. 1.4), and neither IT park employers nor their employees pay the percentage health premium on salaries (Law 1593/2002 art. 4(1^1)). Independent entrepreneurs under chapter 10^4 of the Fiscal Code pay both inside their 15% / 35% single tax (annex 1 pt. 1.10; Fiscal Code art. 69^25).
- Income tax is in [moldova-income-tax](moldova-income-tax.md); the monthly payroll run is in [moldova-payroll](moldova-payroll.md).

## The taxable base

**Social insurance.** The employer rate applies to the total of salaries and rewards calculated each month for all employees (annex 1 pt. 1.1). The monthly base for each employee may not be lower than the minimum wage (MDL 6,300 in 2026), in proportion to the time worked. For an employee on part-time or reduced hours, the contribution may not be less than 25% of the contribution on the minimum wage: at 24%, MDL 1,512 a month at full time and MDL 378 at the 25% floor. Article 22 sets a minimum base only; its former paragraphs (2) and (3) are repealed (Law 489/1999 art. 22(1)). No contribution is calculated on the items in annex 3 to Law 489/1999, which include: dividends, interest and other income from property (pt. 21); sick pay (pt. 19); social benefits from public budgets (pt. 20); business-trip and other compensation, except pay for unused leave on dismissal (pt. 3); severance pay within Labour Code limits (pt. 8); copyright payments and civil contracts other than contracts for works or services (pt. 26); grants and free financial aid (pt. 25); union or employer-body aid up to one average monthly wage a year (pt. 28); and employer payments for child care up to MDL 2,500 a month per child under 3 (pt. 42).

**Health insurance.** The 9% premium is calculated on salary and other rewards before taxes and other deductions are withheld (Law 1593/2002 art. 6). "Other rewards" means any sum other than salary paid by the employer to the employee, and other rights and income paid to individuals, except income under Fiscal Code art. 20, 89, 90 and 90^1 (art. 3). The employer does not pay a health premium of its own; the employee is the payer (annex 1 pt. 2).

**Fixed amounts.** The fixed social contribution is paid as 1/12 each month (annex 1 pt. 1.6, 1.6^1). Patent holders pay at least 1/12 for each month of activity (pt. 1.7). The fixed health premium covers people who are in an annex 2 category on 1 January; someone who joins a category after 31 March pays a pro rata premium within 30 days (Law 1593/2002 art. 22(1), 23(1)). A person who paid the fixed health premium and then pays more than that amount as the 9% premium in the same year may ask CNAM for a refund of the fixed premium (art. 23(2), (2^1)). Moldovan citizens outside every category who prove more than 183 days abroad become insured after paying the full MDL 12,636 (LP321/2025 art. 4(5)).

**Income tax link.** Health premiums and social contributions paid by an individual are deductible for income tax (Fiscal Code art. 35^2(1)-(2)).

| What | Deadline | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Employer social insurance (pt. 1.1-1.5, 1.9) | monthly, by the 25th of the following month | Law 489/1999 annex 1 |
| Fixed social contribution (pt. 1.6, 1.6^1) | 1/12 of the annual sum each month, by the 25th of the following month | annex 1 |
| Patent holders | when the patent is issued or extended | annex 1 pt. 1.7 |
| 9% health premium withheld from pay | by the 25th of the month after the month of payment | Law 1593/2002 art. 12, 20(1) |
| Fixed health premium | in full by 31 March 2026; joiners after that date within 30 days | Law 1593/2002 art. 22(1), 23(1) |
| Monthly return of income tax, health premiums and social contributions (employers) | by the 25th of the month after the payments | Fiscal Code art. 92(2) |
| Independent entrepreneurs | inside the monthly single tax, by the 25th of the following month | annex 1 pt. 1.10; Fiscal Code art. 69^26(2) |

## Penalties and interest

| Breach | Penalty | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Social contributions paid late | 0.1% of the debt for each day of delay, to the day of payment | LP320/2025 art. 4; Law 489/1999 art. 28(1) |
| Contributions or premiums reduced by false data in a return | 20% to 30% of the amount reduced (not applied to a self-corrected return) | Fiscal Code art. 261(4), (4^1) |
| Evading calculation and payment of contributions or premiums | 80% to 100% of the undeclared amount | Fiscal Code art. 261(5) |
| Return not filed or filed wrongly | MDL 200 to 400 or MDL 500 to 1,000 per return (caps MDL 2,000 and MDL 10,000) | Fiscal Code art. 260(1) |

No late penalty is charged on social contributions while a transfer or offset request is being processed, or on debts written off and held on special record by the SFS (Law 489/1999 art. 28(1^1)). The SFS collects unpaid percentage health premiums like tax arrears; CNAM's territorial agencies track the fixed premiums and may agree a payment plan (Law 1593/2002 art. 17). Health premiums and their penalties are time-barred after 3 years (art. 17(4)).

## Cross-border points

- **Foreign workers.** Foreigners with a Moldovan employment contract, permanent residents, beneficiaries of protection and asylum seekers pay health premiums like Moldovan citizens, unless a treaty provides otherwise. Foreigners with temporary residence for family reunion, study, volunteering, religious work or as digital nomads pay like individually insured citizens (Law 1593/2002 art. 10(1)-(2)). Digital nomads become insured after paying the full fixed premium (LP321/2025 art. 4(6)).
- **Moldovans working abroad.** Citizens outside every payer category who prove more than 183 days abroad in the year may insure by paying MDL 12,636 (LP321/2025 art. 4(5)).
- **International projects.** Moldovan citizens employed by international organisations and projects are in pt. 1.1 unless a treaty exempts them (annex 1 pt. 1.1; annex 3 pt. 6).
- **Social security agreements.** Bilateral agreements decide which country's system applies to posted workers; they are not covered in this pack yet (see [md-cross-border](md-cross-border.md) for income tax).

## Worked examples

**Example 1. Private-sector employee, MDL 18,000 a month.** A private company pays an employee MDL 18,000 gross in October 2026. The company owes 24% social insurance, MDL 4,320, on top of the salary. It withholds the employee's 9% health premium, MDL 1,620. Both, with the income tax withheld, are paid and reported by 25 November 2026. The company's cost is MDL 22,320, and MDL 5,940 goes to the two funds.

```oa-check
name: Moldova employer social and employee health, MDL 18,000, 2026
inputs:
  gross: 18000
  employer_social_rate: 0.24
  health_rate: 0.09
steps:
  - employer_social: gross * employer_social_rate
  - employee_health: gross * health_rate
  - employer_cost: gross + employer_social
  - to_funds: employer_social + employee_health
expected:
  employer_social: 4320
  employee_health: 1620
  employer_cost: 22320
  to_funds: 5940
```

**Example 2. Founder of an individual enterprise, paying early or late.** A sole trader who founded an individual enterprise is not a pensioner and has no disability. For 2026 she owes the fixed social contribution of MDL 22,878, paid as MDL 1,906.50 a month by the 25th of the following month. For health insurance she is in annex 2 pt. 1 b). If she pays the fixed premium by 31 March 2026 it is MDL 2,527; paid later it is MDL 12,636. Paying on time saves MDL 10,109. With the early premium her two fixed amounts total MDL 25,405 for the year.

```oa-check
name: Moldova IE founder fixed contributions, 2026
inputs:
  social_fixed: 22878
  health_fixed_full: 12636
  health_fixed_by_31_march: 2527
steps:
  - social_monthly: social_fixed / 12
  - saving_if_paid_by_31_march: health_fixed_full - health_fixed_by_31_march
  - total_paid_on_time: social_fixed + health_fixed_by_31_march
expected:
  social_monthly: 1906.50
  saving_if_paid_by_31_march: 10109
  total_paid_on_time: 25405
```

## Ask the client first

1. Are you an employer, an employee, or self-employed? If self-employed, under which form: individual enterprise, farm, patent, retail trader, justice profession, family doctor, independent entrepreneur?
2. Is the employer private or a public body, and does any job fall under the special working conditions list (annex 2 to Law 489/1999)?
3. Is the business agricultural, with at least 70% of its activity in CAEM groups 01.1 to 01.6?
4. Are you a pensioner or a person with a disability?
5. Is the business an IT park resident?
6. Did you pay the fixed health premium by 31 March?

old_topic_destinations.original_text: **Social insurance.** The employer rate applies to the total of salaries and rewards calculated each month for all employees (annex 1 pt. 1.1). The monthly base for each employee may not be lower than the minimum wage (MDL 6,300 in 2026), in proportion to the time worked. For an employee on part-time or reduced hours, the contribution may not be less than 25% of the contribution on the minimum wage: at 24%, MDL 1,512 a month at full time and MDL 378 at the 25% floor. # Moldova: payroll for employers (2026) v0.2

An employer in Moldova withholds income tax and the employee's health insurance premium from each salary payment and pays its own state social insurance contribution on top. All three are paid and reported to the State Tax Service (SFS) by the 25th of the following month. Figures below are from the Fiscal Code consolidated to Law LP235/2026, Law 489/1999 (annex 1 as replaced for 2026), Law 1593/2002, the 2026 health insurance funds law (LP321/2025) and the 2026 Government decisions on wages.

## Who this applies to

- **Employers**: every employer that pays an employee salary, bonuses and benefits must calculate and withhold income tax (Fiscal Code art. 88(1)). The same rule applies to a beneficiary of works and to a dual-education unit (art. 88(1^2)).
- **Treated as salary**: income of an individual without a business from services or works, fees of board and audit-committee members (art. 88(5)), a director's mandate with a company (art. 88(6)), and an independent entrepreneur working for a client outside the conditions of art. 24(11^1) (art. 88(8)).
- **Employees** are the payers of the 9% health premium (Law 1593/2002 annex 1 pt. 2). They pay no state social insurance contribution; Law 489/1999 annex 1 pt. 1.1 has an employer line only.
- **Day labourers** under Law 22/2018: 12% income tax with no exemptions (art. 15 a1)) and 6% social insurance paid by the beneficiary (Law 489/1999 annex 1 pt. 1.9).
- **IT park residents** pay a 7% single tax that includes salary income tax, employer social contributions and employees' health premiums. Their employees' salaries are taxed finally, without exemptions (Fiscal Code art. 370, 372(1), 377(1)-(2); Law 1593/2002 art. 4(1^1)). See [moldova-tax-optimization](moldova-tax-optimization.md).
- Not here: the annual return and other income (see [moldova-income-tax](moldova-income-tax.md)); fixed contributions of the self-employed (see [moldova-social-contributions](moldova-social-contributions.md)).

## Rates, bands and thresholds

| Item | Rate or amount | Year | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Income tax on salary | 12% | 2026 | Fiscal Code art. 15 a), 88, https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=157050&lang=ro |
| Personal exemption, if annual taxable income is below MDL 360,000 | MDL 29,700 a year | 2026 | art. 33(1), same URL |
| Higher personal exemption (groups in art. 33(2)) | MDL 34,620 a year | 2026 | art. 33(2), same URL |
| Spouse of a person in art. 33(2) | MDL 21,780 a year | 2026 | art. 34(2), same URL |
| Each dependant | MDL 9,900 a year (MDL 21,780 for a childhood or severe disability) | 2026 | art. 35(1), same URL |
| Health premium withheld from the employee | 9.0% of salary and other rewards | 2026 | Law LP321/2025 art. 4(1), https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=156542&lang=ro |
| Employer social insurance, private sector, higher education and medical institutions | 24% | 2026 | Law 489/1999 annex 1 pt. 1.1, https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=156677&lang=ro |
| Employer social insurance, public bodies | 29% | 2026 | annex 1 pt. 1.1, same URL |
| Special working conditions: private / public | 32% / 39% | 2026 | annex 1 pt. 1.2, same URL |
| Agricultural employers (70% test) | 18% employer + 6% state budget | 2026 | annex 1 pt. 1.5, same URL |
| Day labourers' social insurance, paid by the beneficiary | 6% of daily pay | 2026 | annex 1 pt. 1.9, same URL |
| Minimum social insurance base per employee | the minimum wage, in proportion to time worked; part-time or reduced hours: at least 25% of the contribution on the minimum wage | 2026 | Law 489/1999 art. 22(1), same URL |
| Minimum wage, full time (169 hours a month on average) | MDL 6,300 a month, MDL 37.28 an hour | from 1 Jan 2026 | Government Decision 771/2025, https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=152064&lang=ro |
| Forecast average monthly wage | MDL 17,400 | 2026 | Government Decision 773/2025, https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=152066&lang=ro |

## The taxable base

**Order of the calculation.**
1. Start from gross salary, including bonuses and benefits from the employer (art. 88(1); art. 18 c)).
2. Health premium: 9% of salary and other rewards before any tax is withheld (Law 1593/2002 art. 6).
3. Income tax: the employer calculates the tax taking account of the exemptions the employee claimed and of deductions, by the method set by the Government (art. 88(1)). The employee's health premium is a deduction (art. 35^2(1)). Over the year, tax = 12% x (gross pay - health premiums - exemptions claimed).
4. Employer social insurance: the employer's rate applies to the full monthly salaries and rewards (Law 489/1999 annex 1 pt. 1.1). It is not deducted from the employee's pay. The monthly base for each employee may not be lower than the minimum wage, in proportion to time worked; for part-time or reduced hours, the contribution is at least 25% of the contribution on the minimum wage (Law 489/1999 art. 22(1)). At 24% that is MDL 1,512 a month at full time and at least MDL 378 for part-time.

**Exemptions are claimed by application.** To get exemptions, the employee gives the employer a signed application, with copies of the supporting documents, no later than the first day of work. An employee who stays with the same employer does not reapply each year, unless he gains or loses a right. When the exemption amount changes during the year, the employee files a new application within 10 days. The application may be on paper or electronic (art. 88(2)-(3)). Spouse and dependant exemptions start in the month after the right arises (art. 34(3), 35(4)).

**The MDL 360,000 limit.** The personal exemption is only for residents whose annual taxable income is below MDL 360,000 (art. 33(1)). The employer is not required to track whether an employee loses the right to the personal exemption (art. 88(1)). An employee who used the exemption and earned more than MDL 360,000 must file an annual return and pay the difference (art. 83(2) a2), 87(1)).

**What is not in the social insurance base.** No contribution is due on the items in annex 3 to Law 489/1999, for example sick pay, business-trip expenses and other compensation (but pay for unused leave on dismissal is included), severance pay within Labour Code limits, employer-organised transport, meals and training under Government rules, employer payments for child care up to MDL 2,500 a month per child under 3, and dividends.

**Minimum wage.** Full-time pay may not be below MDL 6,300 a month for 169 hours on average. For a legal working week under 40 hours, the hourly minimum is the monthly minimum divided by the average monthly hours of that schedule (Government Decision 771/2025 pt. 1).

| Breach | Penalty | Source |

| Late payment of withheld tax | interest for each day; 11% a year for 2026 | Fiscal Code art. 228(2)-(3) |
| Late payment of social contributions | 0.1% of the debt for each day | LP320/2025 art. 4; Law 489/1999 art. 28 |

## Cross-border points

- **Non-resident employees.** Art. 71(1) n) covers salaries and similar pay of non-resident individuals under an employment contract, and payments to administrators, founders and board or management members of a resident; art. 71(1) o) covers benefits under art. 19 given to non-resident individuals by a resident employer or a permanent establishment. The 12% non-resident withholding in art. 91(1) does not apply to this income when tax is withheld under art. 88 (art. 91(2) b)). When that income comes from a payer that is not a withholding agent, it is taxed at the art. 15 a) rate with no deductions or exemptions (art. 74(1)).
- **Foreign staff and health insurance.** Foreigners with a Moldovan employment contract pay the health premium like Moldovan citizens unless a treaty provides otherwise (Law 1593/2002 art. 10(1)).
- **International organisations.** Moldovan citizens employed by international projects and organisations are covered by employer social insurance unless a treaty exempts them (Law 489/1999 annex 1 pt. 1.1; annex 3 pt. 6).
- **Posted workers and treaties**: treaty relief on employment income is in the pack's cross-border skill, [md-cross-border](md-cross-border.md); social security agreements are not covered yet.

## Worked examples

**Example 1. Standard employee, MDL 20,000 a month.** A private company pays a resident employee MDL 20,000 gross every month of 2026, MDL 240,000 for the year. The employee claimed the personal exemption only. The health premium is 9%, MDL 21,600 a year (MDL 1,800 a month). Income tax for the year is 12% of 240,000 - 21,600 - 29,700 = MDL 188,700, so MDL 22,644 (MDL 1,887 a month if spread evenly). Net pay is MDL 195,756 a year (MDL 16,313 a month). The company pays 24% social insurance, MDL 57,600 a year (MDL 4,800 a month), so the employee costs MDL 297,600. Each month's tax, premium and contribution are paid and reported by the 25th of the next month.

**Example 2. High earner over the MDL 360,000 limit.** An employee earns MDL 35,000 a month, MDL 420,000 in 2026, and claimed the personal exemption at the start of the year. The employer applied it all year, as it is not required to track the loss of the right (art. 88(1)), and withheld 12% of 420,000 - 37,800 - 29,700 = MDL 352,500, so MDL 42,300. But her taxable income after the health premium is MDL 382,200, above MDL 360,000, so she has no right to the exemption (art. 33(1)). Her true tax is 12% of 382,200 = MDL 45,864. ## Ask the client first

1. Is the employer private, a public body, an agricultural business (70% test) or an IT park resident?
2. Does any job fall under the special working conditions list?
3. For each person: employment contract, director's mandate, civil contract for services, or day labourer? Monthly gross pay?
4. Which exemptions has each employee claimed in writing, and is anyone likely to earn MDL 360,000 or more in the year?
5. Are any staff non-resident or foreign nationals, or working for an international project?
6. Does pay include benefits, bonuses, meals, transport or child-care payments?

# Moldova: VAT (TVA) (2026) v2.1

Moldova's VAT (taxa pe valoarea adăugată, TVA) is in Title III of the Fiscal Code and is collected by the State Tax Service (SFS). The tax period is the calendar month. Figures below are from the consolidated Fiscal Code on legis.md as amended to Law LP235 of 2 October 2026 (in force 30 October 2026), and from the two 2026 changes to the registration threshold.

## Who this applies to

- **Taxable subjects** (art. 94): businesses and individuals carrying on business, and non-residents with a permanent establishment in Moldova, who are or must be registered for VAT; anyone importing goods (except individuals importing goods for personal use within the legal limit); anyone importing services, registered or not (except social-political organisations); non-residents without a legal form in Moldova who supply electronic services to Moldovan individuals without a business; and buyers of property from VAT-registered businesses in insolvency, or of pledged, mortgaged or seized property.
- **Taxable transactions** (art. 95(1)): supplies of goods and services by taxable subjects as a result of their business in Moldova, imports of goods, imports of services, electronic services by non-residents to Moldovan consumers, and the property purchases above.
- **Registration is compulsory** for a business whose supplies in any 12 consecutive months exceed the threshold (art. 112(1)). Not counted: supplies exempt without the right to deduct and transactions outside the scope of VAT under art. 95(2).
- **Not required to register**: independent entrepreneurs under chapter 10^4 of Title II, and public authorities and institutions under art. 51 other than public education institutions (art. 112(1)).
- **Out of this skill**: excise duties and customs duty; the IT park and small-company regimes, which do not replace VAT (see [md-corporate-income-tax](md-corporate-income-tax.md) and [moldova-tax-optimization](moldova-tax-optimization.md)).

## Rates, bands and thresholds

| Item | Rate or amount | Year | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Registration threshold, supplies in any 12 consecutive months | MDL 1,500,000 (1 January to 28 February 2026) | 2026 | Fiscal Code art. 112(1), (4) as amended by Law LP318/2025 art. I pct. 14 and art. XIII(1), https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=153700&lang=ro |
| Registration threshold, from 1 March 2026 | MDL 1,700,000 | 2026 | Law LP12/2026 art. I-II, https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=153159&lang=ro; Fiscal Code art. 112(1), https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=157050&lang=ro |
| Threshold in the 2025 text, for comparison | MDL 1,200,000 | 2025 | Fiscal Code version in force 30.12.2025, https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=152857&lang=ro |
| Standard rate | 20% of the taxable value of imports and of supplies in Moldova | 2026 | Fiscal Code art. 96 a) |
| Reduced rate: bread and bakery products; milk and dairy products (fat up to 40%) | 8% | 2026 | art. 96 b) |
| Reduced rate: registered medicines, magistral preparations, listed medical goods | 8% | 2026 | art. 96 b) |
| Reduced rate: natural gas, liquefied gas (2711), gas transport and distribution | 8% | 2026 | art. 96 b) |
| Reduced rate: listed livestock, crop and horticultural produce in natural form; beet sugar; solid biofuel | 8% | 2026 | art. 96 b) |
| Reduced rate: accommodation (hotels, motels, guesthouses, campsites and similar) and food and non-alcoholic drinks served for immediate consumption, in CAEM section I | 8% | 2026 | art. 96 b) |
| Reduced rate: tampons, sanitary pads, menstrual cups | 8% | 2026 | art. 96 b) |
| Pro rata de minimis: exempt-without-deduction share below which all common input VAT is deductible | 0.05 | 2026 | art. 102(4) |
| Fine for not issuing a tax invoice on time | MDL 3,000 to 3,600 per invoice, up to MDL 72,000 | 2026 | art. 260(4) |
| Late-payment interest | 11% a year, per day | 2026 | art. 228(3); NBM base rate 6.00% on 6 Nov 2025, https://www.bnm.md/ro/content/raportul-asupra-inflatiei-nr-4-2025 |

## The taxable base

**Exempt with the right to deduct** (art. 104), the Moldovan equivalent of zero rating: exports of goods and services; international transport of goods and passengers, including forwarding, international gas transport and listed airport and aircraft services; electricity, heat, hot water, water supply and sewerage for residential property; imports of natural gas, electricity and heat through networks; goods and services for technical-assistance and grant-funded projects listed by the Government; supplies into, out of and between free economic zones, the Giurgiulești port and the Mărculești airport, with exceptions for transport services and balancing energy; and listed processing services under inward processing. A tax invoice is not required for supplies under art. 104 a) (art. 117(1)).

**Exempt without the right to deduct** (art. 103(1)), main items: housing, land, residential lettings and land leases (but not agency commissions); listed baby food; privatised state property; education services of public and private institutions; state-fee services; care of the sick and elderly; medical services other than cosmetic, and medical raw materials; financial services, including insurance and reinsurance and insurance intermediation (pt. 12 g)); postal services; gambling; funeral services; residential accommodation in hostels and communal services to the population; domestic passenger transport; books and periodicals (not advertising or erotic); listed farm machinery, hail rockets, small hydro turbines and renewable-energy works; and certain cars and other vehicles in tariff headings 8703 as listed. Input VAT on purchases used for these supplies is not deductible and goes to cost (art. 102(2)).

**Time of supply** (art. 108). VAT is due on the date of supply. For goods, that is the date of handover to the buyer, or the date transport starts; for exports, the date the goods leave Moldova. For real estate, it is the date of entry in the real-estate register. For services, it is the date the service is performed, the invoice is issued or payment is received, whichever is first. If an invoice is issued or payment received before the supply, the earlier of those dates applies. For regular supplies under a contract (electricity, heat, water, gas, rent, lettings), it is the date of delivery or of each regular payment, whichever is first. For leasing, it is the payment date in the contract, or the date an advance is received. For construction, consulting, research, expert work and similar services paid in stages, it is the date of the handover document, or of acceptance by the customer if the contract says so (art. 108(1)-(8)).

**Imports.** Imports of goods are taxed at customs (art. 95(1) b), 100). Imports of services are taxed in Moldova: the buyer calculates VAT on the service, declares it and pays it (art. 95(1) c), 101(1)). A buyer who is not VAT-registered declares and pays VAT on imported services by the 25th of the month after the month the service was imported or paid, whichever is earlier (art. 115(2) b)). A registered buyer deducts the VAT it calculated on imported services used for taxable supplies (art. 102(1)). Imported services count toward the registration threshold (art. 112(4)).

**Place of supply of services** (art. 111): where the property is, for real-estate services, construction and accommodation; along the route, for transport; where performed, for services on movable goods, culture, education, sport, entertainment and transport-related services; where used, for hire of movable goods; and where the customer is established, for intellectual property, advertising, consulting, engineering, legal, accounting and marketing services, translation, information services, IT services delivered electronically, staffing, and agents acting for these. Electronic communications, broadcasting and radio services are also supplied where the customer is (art. 111(2)).

**Electronic services to consumers.** A non-resident without a legal form in Moldova that supplies services through electronic networks (software and databases, online advertising, marketplaces, hosting, data storage, domain names and similar, art. 95(1^1)) to Moldovan individuals without a business registers under art. 112^1, files quarterly and pays in MDL, USD or EUR (art. 94 d), 114(1^1), 115(1^2), (3)).

**Input VAT deduction** (art. 102). A VAT-registered business deducts VAT paid or payable to VAT-registered suppliers on goods and services bought for taxable supplies in its business. VAT on imported goods is deductible only once paid. VAT on purchases used for both taxable and exempt-without-deduction supplies is deducted by a monthly pro rata, rounded to two decimals: taxable supplies divided by taxable plus exempt-without-deduction supplies, without VAT and excluding advances. A final pro rata on the year's figures is applied in the last return of the year. If the exempt-without-deduction share is below 0.05, all of the common input VAT is deductible (art. 102(3)-(4)). VAT on purchases not used for the business, on goods stolen or lost beyond the limits set by management, and on the undepreciated value of written-off fixed assets, is not deductible (art. 102(8)).

**Excess input VAT.** When input VAT for a month is higher than output VAT, the difference is carried forward to the next tax period and added to that period's input VAT (art. 101(2)). It is refunded instead in three cases: to producers of bread and bakery products and of milk and dairy products, within the difference between the standard and the reduced rate (art. 101(3)); where the excess arises from supplies exempt with the right to deduct, such as exports (art. 101(5)); and to leasing companies, for the excess on supplies under leasing contracts (art. 101(6)).

**Deregistration.** When registration is cancelled, the business is treated as supplying its stock and the fixed assets on which it deducted VAT, at market value (for depreciable assets, the higher of book and market value), and pays VAT on that supply (art. 113(3)). The SFS may cancel a registration itself when no returns are filed or the address is false (art. 113(2)).

## Deadlines and filing

| What | Deadline | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Notify the SFS and register after exceeding the threshold | by the last day of the month in which the threshold was exceeded; registered from the first day of the following month | art. 112(1) |
| Voluntary registration | registered from the first day of the month after the application | art. 112(2) |
| Registration before buying goods under art. 110(4) | before the purchase | art. 112(4^1) |
| Reorganisation notice | within 5 working days of state registration of the new entities | art. 112(5) |
| Tax period | one calendar month; one calendar quarter for non-resident e-service suppliers | art. 114(1), (1^1) |
| VAT return | by the 25th of the month after the period, filed electronically | art. 115(1), (1^1) |
| Payment | by the return deadline; import-related services at import; imported services of non-registered buyers by the 25th of the following month | art. 115(2) |
| Tax invoice | at the time the tax obligation arises under art. 108; e-invoice (e-factura) for businesses on the SFS list and for public-procurement contracts | art. 117(1), (1^1), (1^2) |

## Penalties and interest

| Breach | Penalty | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Late payment | interest for each day; 11% a year for 2026 (NBM base rate 6% + 5 points) | art. 228(2)-(3) |
| Tax invoice not issued on time (also for exempt-without-deduction supplies) | MDL 3,000 to 3,600 per invoice, up to MDL 72,000 | art. 260(4) |
| Return not filed or filed wrongly | MDL 200 to 400 or MDL 500 to 1,000 per return (caps MDL 2,000 and MDL 10,000) | art. 260(1) |
| VAT reduced by false data in a return | 20% to 30% of the amount reduced (not applied to a self-corrected return) | art. 261(4), (4^1) |
| Evading calculation and payment | 80% to 100% of the undeclared amount | art. 261(5) |
| Refund paid above the correct amount | interest from the refund date until recovered | art. 228(10) |

The SFS may cancel the registration of a business that files no returns (art. 113(2) b)). Assessments are time-barred after 4 years, up to 6 years where no return was filed or a refund is claimed (art. 264).

## Cross-border points

- **Exports** are exempt with the right to deduct (art. 104 a)), so input VAT on them stays deductible.
- **Services bought from abroad** are taxed in Moldova when the place of supply is Moldova under art. 111; the Moldovan buyer self-assesses (art. 95(1) c), 101(1)). For consulting, IT, advertising and similar services, the place of supply is where the customer is established (art. 111(1) e)).
- **Services sold abroad**: the same rule makes consulting, IT, advertising and similar services supplied to a foreign business customer supplied outside Moldova.
- **Non-resident e-service suppliers** to Moldovan consumers register, file quarterly and may pay in MDL, USD or EUR (art. 94 d), 114(1^1), 115(3)).
- **Energy from foreign sellers.** A registered buyer of network gas, electricity or heat from a seller not established in Moldova enters the VAT as both output and input VAT on receipt of the invoice (art. 101(1^1)).
- **Free economic zones, Giurgiulești port and Mărculești airport** have their own exemptions with deduction (art. 104 f), f1), i)).

## Worked examples

**Example 1. Monthly return, October 2026.** A VAT-registered food shop sells MDL 300,000 (net) of household goods at 20% and MDL 50,000 (net) of bread at 8% in October 2026. Its purchases for the business carry MDL 30,000 of VAT on valid tax invoices. Output VAT is MDL 60,000 + MDL 4,000 = MDL 64,000. Input VAT is MDL 30,000. It pays MDL 34,000 and files the October return by 25 November 2026.

```oa-check
name: Moldova monthly VAT return, 20% and 8%, October 2026
inputs:
  sales_standard: 300000
  sales_reduced: 50000
  input_vat: 30000
  standard_rate: 0.20
  reduced_rate: 0.08
steps:
  - output_standard: sales_standard * standard_rate
  - output_reduced: sales_reduced * reduced_rate
  - output_total: output_standard + output_reduced
  - payable: output_total - input_vat
expected:
  output_standard: 60000
  output_reduced: 4000
  output_total: 64000
  payable: 34000
```

**Example 2. Mixed taxable and exempt supplies, with an imported service.** A registered company lets commercial premises (taxable at 20%) for MDL 800,000 and residential flats (exempt without deduction) for MDL 200,000 in a month. Common running costs carry MDL 50,000 of input VAT. The exempt share is 0.20, above 0.05, so the pro rata applies: 800,000 / 1,000,000 = 0.80, and MDL 40,000 is deductible; MDL 10,000 goes to cost (art. 102(4)). The company also buys legal advice for the commercial lettings from a foreign law firm for MDL 10,000. The place of supply is Moldova (art. 111(1) e)), so the company calculates VAT of MDL 2,000 as output and deducts it as input (art. 101(1), 102(1)). Output VAT is MDL 162,000, input VAT MDL 42,000, and MDL 120,000 is payable.

```oa-check
name: Moldova VAT pro rata with imported service, 2026
inputs:
  taxable_supplies: 800000
  exempt_supplies: 200000
  common_input_vat: 50000
  imported_service: 10000
  rate: 0.20
steps:
  - exempt_share: exempt_supplies / (taxable_supplies + exempt_supplies)
  - pro_rata: round(taxable_supplies / (taxable_supplies + exempt_supplies), 2)
  - deductible_common: common_input_vat * pro_rata
  - to_cost: common_input_vat - deductible_common
  - reverse_charge_vat: imported_service * rate
  - output_vat: taxable_supplies * rate + reverse_charge_vat
  - input_vat: deductible_common + reverse_charge_vat
  - payable: output_vat - input_vat
expected:
  exempt_share: 0.20
  pro_rata: 0.80
  deductible_common: 40000
  to_cost: 10000
  reverse_charge_vat: 2000
  output_vat: 162000
  input_vat: 42000
  payable: 120000
```

## Ask the client first

1. Are you VAT-registered? If not, what were your supplies in each of the last 12 months, and do you buy services from abroad?
2. What do you sell: which goods or services, and do any fall under the 8% list, art. 103 (exempt) or art. 104 (exports and other exempt-with-deduction supplies)?
3. Do you sell to or buy from customers and suppliers abroad, and are your customers businesses or consumers?
4. Do you make both taxable and exempt supplies, so that the pro rata applies?
5. Are you on the SFS list for compulsory e-invoices, or do you have public-procurement contracts?
6. Are you in a free economic zone, the Giurgiulești port or the Mărculești airport?
7. Do you have excess input VAT carried forward from earlier months, or a refund claim open?

old_topic_destinations.original_text: **Time of supply** (art. 108). VAT is due on the date of supply. For goods, that is the date of handover to the buyer, or the date transport starts; for exports, the date the goods leave Moldova. For real estate, it is the date of entry in the real-estate register. For services, it is the date the service is performed, the invoice is issued or payment is received, whichever is first. If an invoice is issued or payment received before the supply, the earlier of those dates applies. For regular supplies under a contract (electricity, heat, water, gas, rent, lettings), it is the date of delivery or of each regular payment, whichever is first. For leasing, it is the payment date in the contract, or the date an advance is received. For construction, consulting, research, expert work and similar services paid in stages, it is the date of the handover document, or of acceptance by the customer if the contract says so (art. 108(1)-(8)).

old_topic_destinations.original_text: **Imports.** Imports of goods are taxed at customs (art. 95(1) b), 100). Imports of services are taxed in Moldova: the buyer calculates VAT on the service, declares it and pays it (art. 95(1) c), 101(1)). A registered buyer deducts the VAT it calculated on imported services used for taxable supplies (art. 102(1)). Imported services count toward the registration threshold (art. 112(4)).

old_topic_destinations.original_text: **Input VAT deduction** (art. 102). A VAT-registered business deducts VAT paid or payable to VAT-registered suppliers on goods and services bought for taxable supplies in its business. VAT on imported goods is deductible only once paid. VAT on purchases used for both taxable and exempt-without-deduction supplies is deducted by a monthly pro rata, rounded to two decimals: taxable supplies divided by taxable plus exempt-without-deduction supplies, without VAT and excluding advances. A final pro rata on the year's figures is applied in the last return of the year. If the exempt-without-deduction share is below 0.05, all of the common input VAT is deductible (art. 102(3)-(4)). VAT on purchases not used for the business, on goods stolen or lost beyond the limits set by management, and on the undepreciated value of written-off fixed assets, is not deductible (art. 102(8)).

Fixed:
- Deadlines: added art. 83(4) a). Legal persons and resident organisational forms with the status of an individual file by the 25th of the third month (25 March 2027 for 2026). Before this fix the table gave only the 30 April date for individuals and the 25 March date for small IEs and farms under art. 83(11).
- Cross-border: the link to md-cross-border now points at the merged skill (#793). It used to say "in preparation".

Confirmed: 12% (art. 15 a)), day labourers 12% with no exemptions, farms 7%; exemptions 29,700 (below 360,000), 34,620, spouse 21,780, dependants 9,900 / 21,780, dependant income limit 12,400; art. 35^2 deductions, with insurance and first-home interest capped at 17,400 (HG 773/2025) and education at 20,000 from 1 Jan 2026 (LP318 art. XIII). Final withholding: dividends 6% (15% on 2008-2011 profits), bank interest 6%, rent 12% or 7%, royalties 12%, gambling 18% with lottery wins up to 297 not taxed, promotional prizes 12%. Also the retail regime (1%, minimum 3,000 a year, 750 a quarter, 250 a month), the IE regime (15% up to 1.2m, 35% above, 40 activities, in force 1 Jan 2026 by LP228 art. VI), the 30 April and 25 March deadlines, instalments, the art. 260 and 261 fines, 4- and 6-year limitation, and late interest of 11% (NBM 6.00% kept on 6 Nov 2025, plus 5 points).
